payload.text: The Brennecke Institute developed a thalliline-doped sodium-flow battery intended to suppress electrolyte crossover, a key aging mechanism. An independent audit corrected the prototype’s cycle life to 8,400 cycles to the 80% capacity threshold, retracting the earlier 12,000-cycle claim. The cell has a gravimetric energy density of 148 Wh/kg and a projected stack-level cost of $61/kWh at 500 MWh manufacturing scale. Its operating-temperature floor is 4 °C, below which the dopant precipitates and cycling must stop.
